searchText: <@&857649635274915900> Gossipsub uses the first 20bytes of hash of the message data (decompressed/compressed) as `message-id`. `message-id` is the only context peers have to obtain new gossip that they don't already have or want. Historically, the protocol has limited each topic/subnet to a message payload of common interest for everyone subscribed to the topic/subnet. In the case of danksharding, however, there might be multiple custody columns/rows distributed in the same subnet and not all subscribers would be interested in all columns/rows distributed. Would it in this case make sense to add some context to the `message-id`? Can this problem be circumvented in some-other way (like playing around with the custody requirement size and the number of columns/rows)? I guess you mean this part of the specs https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/_features/eip7594/p2p-interface.md#data_column_sidecar_subnet_id Looks like peers are subscribed for the subnets they need = columns Yes, but for full danksharding. the devs played a lot with the custody requirement size on the calls 😁 True that. Usually there is one subnet assigned for one message type (one column in the case of peerDAS). And I'm not sure if having 1024 subnets for full danksharding will be a problem or not Is there a limit to how many subnets we can have on the gossipsub network? I guess 32, as the number of columns for now https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/_features/eip7594/p2p-interface.md#compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar oh no, seems 128 https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/specs/_features/eip7594/das-core.md#networking <@571701739028217885> https://hackmd.io/TSLwFcUMTkynfVtf-a9_Ag#Issue-1-Increase-custody-requirement-and-subnet-count Thank you for the reference There are also notes from Peerdas breakout rooms What you suggest in the second paragraph is indeed something that needs to be considered for 2 dimensional peerDAS. As of now, as we’re using subnet sampling, it’s one DataColumnSidecar per subnet. Also did you check out the type called DataColumnIdentifier from the spec? I believe you are referring to something similar. If I don’t fail to understand. 🙂 Which means, as per alpha 6 of CL specs Number of Columns == Data Column Sidecar Subnet Count

excerpts.content:
<@&857649635274915900> Gossipsub uses the first 20bytes of hash of the message data (decompressed/compressed) as `message-id`. `message-id`  is the only context peers have to obtain new gossip that they don't already have or want. Historically, the protocol has limited each topic/subnet to a message payload of common interest for everyone subscribed to the topic/subnet. 

In the case of danksharding, however, there might be multiple custody columns/rows distributed in the same subnet and not all subscribers would be interested in all columns/rows distributed. Would it in this case make sense to add some context to the `message-id`? Can this problem be circumvented in some-other way (like playing around with the custody requirement size and the number of columns/rows)?
